H268.d: or (shortened) אָחֹר ; from אֲחִירַע; the hinder part; hence (adverb) behind, backward; also (as facing north) the West; after(-ward), back (part, -side, -ward), hereafter, (be-) hind(-er part), time to come, without.

H130.d: or (fully) אֱדוֹמִי ; patronymic from אֱדֹם; See אֲרוֹמִי.; an Edomite, or descendants from (or inhabitants of) Edom; Edomite.

H76.d: (by reduplication) from an unused root (meaning to belch forth); an inflammatory pustule (as eruption); blains.

H438.d: the same as אַלּוֹן; Allon, an Israelite, also a place in Palestine; Allon.

H65.d: from אָבֵל and מְחֹלָהxlit mᵉchôwlâh corrected to mᵉchôlâh; meadow of dancing; Abel-Mecholah, a place in Palestine; Abel-meholah.

H205.d: from an unused root perhaps meaning properly, to pant (hence, to exert oneself, usually in vain; to come to naught); strictly nothingness; also trouble. vanity, wickedness; specifically an idol; affliction, evil, false, idol, iniquity, mischief, mourners(-ing), naught, sorrow, unjust, unrighteous, vain, vanity, wicked(-ness). Compare אַיִן.

H221.d: from אוּר; fiery; Uri, the name of three Israelites; Uri.

H204.d: or (shortened); אֹן; of Egyptian derivation; On, a city of Egypt; On.

H401.d: or אֻכָּל; apparently from אָכַל; devoured; Ucal, a fancy name; Ucal.

H367.d: or (shortened) אֵמָה; from the same as אָיֹם; fright; concrete, an idol (as a bugbear); dread, fear, horror, idol, terrible, terror.
r: me and let not his fear
me and let not thy dread

H486.d: probably of foreign derivation; Almodad, a son of Joktan; Almodad.

H170.d: in form a feminine of אֹהֶל, but in fact for אׇהֳלָהּ; from אֹהֶל; her tent (i.e. idolatrous sanctuary); Oholah, a symbolic name for Samaria; Aholah.

H4.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֵב; {a green plant}; fruit.

H323.d: of Persian derivation; a satrap or governorof amain province (of Persia); lieutenant.

H430.d: plural of אֱלוֹהַּ; gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative; angels, [idiom] exceeding, God (gods) (-dess, -ly), [idiom] (very) great, judges, [idiom] mighty.

H10.d: the same as אֲבֵדָה, miswritten for אֲבַדּוֹן; a perishing; destruction.

H96.d: from an unused root (meaning to flow down or together as drops); a reservoir; drop.

H189.d: probably from אָוָה; desirous; Evi, a Midianitish chief; Evi.

H294.d: from אָח and סָמַךְ; brother of support; Achisamak, an Israelite; Ahisamach.

H457.d: apparently from אַל; good for nothing, by anal. vain or vanity; specifically an idol; idol, no value, thing of nought.

H77.d: from an unused root probably meaning to gleam; conspicuous; Ebets, a place in Palestine; Abez.

H355.d: feminine of אַיָּל; a doe or female deer; hind.

H476.d: from אֵל and שָׁמַע; God of hearing; Elishama, the name of seven Israelites; Elishama.

H192.d: of Aramaic derivation and probably meaning soldier of Merodak; Evil-Merodak, a Babylonian king; Evil-merodach.

H136.d: an emphatic form of אָדוֹן; the Lord (used as a proper name of God only); (my) Lord.

H493.d: from אֵל and נָעֵם; God (is his) delight; Elnaam, an Israelite; Elnaam.

H459.d: (Aramaic) or shorter אִלֵּן; prolonged from אֵל; these; the, these.

H366.d: from an unused root (meaning to frighten); frightful; terrible.

H298.d: patronymic from אֲחִירָם; an Achiramite or descendant (collectively) of Achiram; Ahiramites.

H110.d: probably from אָדַב (in the sense of chastisement) and אֵל; disciplined of God; Adbeel, a son of Ishmael; Adbeel.

H61.d: apparently from אָבַל through the idea of negation; nay, i.e. truly or yet; but, indeed, nevertheless, verily.

H127.d: from אָדַם; soil (from its general redness); country, earth, ground, husband(-man) (-ry), land.

H209.d: a variation of אוֹנוֹ; strong; Onan, a son of Judah; Onan.

H149.d: (Aramaic) probably of Persian origin; quickly or carefully; diligently.

H468.d: xlit ʼĔlêytsûwr corrected to ʼĔlîytsûwr; from אֵל and צוּר; God of (the) rock; Elitsur, an Israelite; Elizur.

H97.d: dual of אֶגֶל.; a double pond; Eglajim, a place in Moab; Eglaim.

H478.d: from אֵל and שָׁפַט; God of judgment; Elishaphat, an Israelite; Elishaphat.

H38.d: from אָב and יָם; father of (the) sea (i.e. seaman); Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah; Abijam.

H302.d: from אָח and תָּפֵל; brother of folly; Achithophel, an Israelite; Ahithophel.

H344.d: perhaps from אִי; the screamer, i.e. a hawk; kite, vulture.

H376.d: contracted for אֱנוֹשׁ (or perhaps rather from an unused root meaning to be extant); a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation); also, another, any (man), a certain, [phrase] champion, consent, each, every (one), fellow, (foot-, husband-) man, (good-, great, mighty) man, he, high (degree), him (that is), husband, man(-kind), [phrase] none, one, people, person, [phrase] steward, what (man) soever, whoso(-ever), worthy. Compare אִשָּׁה.

H304.d: the same as אַחֲלַי; wishful; Achlai, the name of an Israelitess and of an Israelite; Ahlai.

H215.d: a primitive root; to be (causative, make) luminous (literally and metaphorically); [idiom] break of day, glorious, kindle, (be, en-, give, show) light (-en, -ened), set on fire, shine.
r: thereof that they may give light

H29.d: or prolonged אֲבִיָּהוּ ; from אָב and יָהּ; father (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses; Abiah, Abijah.

H207.d: or (shortened) אֹנוֹ; prolonged from אוֹן; strong; Ono, a place in Palestine; Ono.

H211.d: or (shortened) אֹפִיר; and אוֹפִר; of uncertain derivation; Ophir, the name of a son of Joktan, and of a gold region in the East; Ophir.

H472.d: from אֵל and שֶׁבַע (in the sense of שָׁבַע); God of (the) oath; Elisheba, the wife of Aaron; Elisheba.

H421.d: a primitive root (rather identical with אָלָה through the idea of invocation); to bewail; lament.

H251.d: a primitive word; a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance (like father)); another, brother(-ly); kindred, like, other. Compare also the proper names beginning with 'Ah-' or 'Ahi-'.

H455.d: from אֵל and חָבָא; God will hide; Eljachba, an Israelite; Eliahbah.

H190.d: feminine of אוֹי; {lamentation; also interjectionally Oh!}; woe.

H243.d: from אָזַן and תָּבוֹר; flats (i.e. tops) of Tabor (i.e. situated on it); Aznoth-Tabor, a place in Palestine; Aznoth-tabor.

H409.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַל; {not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing}; not.

H379.d: from אִישׁ and הוֹד; man of renown; Ishod, an Israelite; Ishod.

H396.d: feminine from אָכַל; something eatable, i.e. food; meat.

H27.d: from אָב and דִּין; father of judgment (i.e. judge); Abidan, an Israelite; Abidan.

H32.d: or (more correctly) אֲבִיחַיִל ; from אָב and חַיִל; father (i.e. possessor) of might; Abihail or Abichail, the name of three Israelites and two Israelitesses; Abihail.

H171.d: from אֹהֶל and אָב; tent of (his) father; Oholiab, an Israelite; Aholiab.

H377.d: denominative from אִישׁ; to be a man, i.e. act in amanly way; show (one) self a man.

H117.d: from אָדַר; wide or (generally) large; figuratively, powerful; excellent, famous, gallant, glorious, goodly, lordly, mighty(-ier one), noble, principal, worthy.

H247.d: a primitive root; to belt; bind (compass) about, gird (up, with).

H166.d: a primitive root; to be clear; shine.

H178.d: from the same as אָב (apparently through the idea of prattling a father's name); properly, a mumble, i.e. a water skin (from its hollow sound); hence a necromancer (ventriloquist, as from a jar); bottle, familiar spirit.
r: one that hath a familiar spirit

H281.d: or (prolonged) אֲחִיָּהוּ ; from אָח and יָהּ; brother (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Achijah, the name of nine Israelites; Ahiah, Ahijah.

H484.d: probably of foreign derivation (used thus only in the plural); almug (i.e. probably sandle-wood) sticks; almug trees. Compare אַלְגּוּמִּים.

H246.d: a variation for זִיקָה; manacles; chains.

H255.d: probably from אָח; a howler or lonesome wild animal; doleful creature.

H229.d: probably from אֵזוֹב; hyssop-like; Ezbai, an Israelite; Ezbai.

H256.d: once (by contraction) אֶחָב (Jeremiah 29:22); from אָח and אָב; brother (i.e. friend) of (his) father; Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon; Ahab.

H23.d: from אָב and אָסַף; father of gathering (i.e. gatherer); Abiasaph, an Israelite; Abiasaph.

H351.d: probably a variation for אֵיךְ, but not as an interogative; where; where.

H329.d: from an unused root probably meaning to pierce or make fast; a thorn-tree (especially the buckthorn); Atad, bramble, thorn.

H176.d: presumed to be the 'constructive' or genitival form of אַו ; short for אַוָּה; desire (and so probably in Proverbs 31:4); hence (by way of alternative) or, also if; also, and, either, if, at the least, [idiom] nor, or, otherwise, then, whether.

H495.d: probably of foreign derivation; Ellasar, an early country of Asia; Ellasar.

H152.d: from אָדַר and מֶלֶךְ; splendor of (the) king; Adrammelek, the name of an Assyrian idol, also of a son of Sennacherib; Adrammelech.

H111.d: probably an orthographical variation for חֲדַד; Adad (or Hadad), an Edomite; Hadad.

H90.d: or אֲגָג; of uncertain derivation (compare אָגֵא); flame; Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings; Agag.

H331.d: a primitive root; to close (the lips or ears); by analology to contract (a window by bevelled jambs); narrow, shut, stop.

H39.d: from אָב and an elsewhere unused (probably foreign) word; father of Mael (apparently some Arab tribe); Abimael, a son of Joktan; Abimael.

H212.d: or (shortened) אֹפָן; from an unused root meaning to revolve; a wheel; wheel.

H75.d: a primitive root; to fodder; fatted, stalled.

H494.d: from אֵל and נָתַן; God (is the) giver; Elnathan, the name of four Israelites; Elnathan.

H461.d: from אֵל and עֵזֶר; God of help; Eliezer, the name of a Damascene and of ten Israelites; Eliezer.

H105.d: of uncertain derivation; a basin; charger.

H417.d: from אֵל and גָּבִישׁ; hail (as if a great pearl); great hail(-stones).

H466.d: from אֵל and פָּלָה; God of his distinction; Eliphelehu, an Israelite; Elipheleh.

H217.d: from אוֹר; flame; hence (in the plural) the East (as being the region of light); fire, light. See also אוּרִים.

H11.d: intensive from אָבַד; abstract, a perishing; concrete, Hades; destruction.

H112.d: of uncertain derivation; Iddo, an Israelite; Iddo.

H201.d: from אָמַר; talkative; Omar, a grandson of Esau; Omar.

H314.d: or (shortened) אַחֲרֹן; from אָחַר; hinder; generally, late or last; specifically (as facing the east) western; after (-ward), to come, following, hind(-er, -ermost, -most), last, latter, rereward, ut(ter) most.

H168.d: from אָהַל; a tent (as clearly conspicuous from a distance); covering, (dwelling) (place), home, tabernacle, tent.

H147.d: (Aramaic) intensive, from a root corresponding to אָדַר; ample, i.e. a threshing-floor; threshingfloor.

H74.d: or (fully) אֲבִינֵר ; from אָב and נִיר; father of light (i.e. enlightening); Abner, an Israelite; Abner.

H357.d: from אַיָּל; deer-field; Ajalon, the name of five places in Palestine; Aijalon, Ajalon.

H414.d: a variation of אֵלָהlemma אִלָה first vowel, corrected to אֵלָה; oak; Ela, an Israelite; Elah.

H89.d: of uncertain derivation (compare אֲגַג); Age, an Israelite; Agee.

H133.d: probably of Persian derivation; Admatha, a Persian nobleman; Admatha.

H248.d: a variation for זְרוֹעַ; the arm; arm.

H182.d: or (shortened) אֹדוֹת (only thus in the plural); from the same as אוּד; turnings (i.e. occasions); (adverb) on account of; (be-) cause, concerning, sake.

H345.d: the same as אַיָּה; Ajah, the name of two Israelites; Aiah, Ajah.

H134.d: from the same as אָדוֹן (in the sense of strength); a basis (of a building, a column, etc.); foundation, socket.

H415.d: from אֵל and אֱלֹהִים and יִשְׂרָאֵל; the mighty god if Jisrael; El-Elohi-Jisrael, the title given to a consecrated spot by Jacob; Elelohe-israel.

H273.d: from אָחַז; seizer; Achzai, an Israelite; Ahasai.

H219.d: feminine of אוֹר; luminousness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity; also a plant (as being bright); herb, light.

H371.d: apparently a shortened form of אַיִן; but (like אַיִן) an interrogative; is it not?; not.

H45.d: from אָב and an unused root of uncertain derivation; probably, father of strength (i.e. valiant); Abialbon, an Israelite; Abialbon.

H433.d: rarely (shortened) אֱלֹהַּ; probably prolonged (emphatic) from אֵל; a deity or the Deity; God, god. See אֱלֹהִים.

H265.d: by reduplication from אָח; brotherly; Achoach, an Israelite; Ahoah.

H106.d: from גָּרַף (in the sense of grasping); the clenched hand; fist.

H172.d: (similarly with אׇהֳלָה) for אׇהֳלִיבָהּ ; from אֹהֶל; my tent (is) in her; Oholibah, a symbolic name for Judah; Aholibah.
